definition: the five rules I learned as a child that still fire, long after I stopped believing them

settled:
Always be nice, always be quiet, do not take up space, do not ask for anything, take care of yourself.

They run from below thought, so winning the argument against them did not stop them.

They are not merely stuck, though. The beliefs under them are superseded and each now reads as a social cost I still cannot afford, under the rule that if I cannot afford to, I am not allowed to.

Two more came out of the same world and I broke both: do what other people tell you to, and follow all of the rules. At some point the weight of expectations got so heavy that I took up a blanket rebellion against all of them, other people's and my own alike. What replaced the two is that if I do not want to, I am not allowed to.

So a rule I chose has two installed rules for ancestors.

Most of the seven point one way: shrink the target, make less of me for a random punishment to land on. Keeping my word is the one active member, being flawless on the piece of the surface I can control.

title: The Five Rules I Grew Up With
